title: He Said Every Request Needs A Ticket. I Made Everything A Ticket.
script: Our new IT director got tired of people pinging him directly for small fixes, so he sent out a memo: every single request, no matter how small, must go through the ticket system, no verbal exceptions, or it simply would not get done. I complied completely. I filed a ticket when my monitor flickered. I filed a ticket when his own badge reader jammed because of a policy he wrote. I filed a ticket about the ticket system being slow to load tickets. Within two weeks the queue had over six hundred open items, and executives who wanted a two minute fix were stuck waiting behind a backlog his own rule created. He tried quietly fixing things off the books again, and I reminded him, politely, that verbal requests were against policy. Regional finally asked why simple fixes were taking three weeks. He had no good answer, because the answer was him.
